subject: Hosted API commit increase and rate-limit tier coordination
message_1_subject: Request: increase hosted commit & higher burst rate for Q3
message_1_body:
Hi Sofia,

Quick note — our forecasts for Q3 show a 2.5x increase in traffic for our recommendations service. We hit several rate limits during the June sale and it caused visible latency spikes. Can we discuss (a) raising our monthly commit from 1M to 2.5M tokens, and (b) temporary increased burst rate for the month of Sept? We’d like to understand pricing/discounts that would apply if we commit to a higher tier for 12 months.

I attached a short forecast table for reference.

Thanks,
Heather
Director, Platform Ops
Acme Retail

Attachment: ACME_Q3_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
message_2_subject: Re: Request: increase hosted commit & higher burst rate for Q3
message_2_body:
Hi Heather — thanks for the heads-up and the forecast. I’ve looped in Ben from account exec. High level: we can support a 2.5x commit uplift, and we have two pricing pathways — a straight monthly commit increase with tiered per-token rates, or a committed 12-month uplift with an additional volume discount and guaranteed burst headroom.

Ben — can you pull a couple of concrete pricing examples (monthly vs 12-month) and confirm whether we can offer a temporary enhanced burst window for Sept (one-time fee or included in the tier)? Also copying in Stephanie from Customer Success to coordinate a short runbook for the Sept sale so we minimize cache misses.

Heather — I reviewed the attached forecast; thanks. I’ll get back with numbers by EOD tomorrow.

—Sofia
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Pricing options: 2.5x commit vs 12-month uplift — ACME
message_3_body:
Hi Heather / Sofia,

Thanks — I put together two straightforward options based on the forecast: 

Option A — Month-to-month steeped tier (no term)
- New monthly commit: 2,500,000 tokens
- Effective per-token price: $0.00033 (same as current tier pricing scaled up)
- Burst window: up to 3x baseline for 72 hours — one-time surge fee = $2,500

Option B — 12-month committed uplift
- Committed monthly: 2,500,000 tokens (12-month term)
- Effective per-token price: $0.00028 (6% discount vs Option A overall)
- Burst window: up to 4x baseline for 7 days per quarter, included
- SLA: 99.9% availability for hosted endpoints; priority capacity during rolling upgrades

I also attached a draft amendment (commit_amendment_redline.pdf) with the language for the tier increase and burst terms. Two asks: (1) Heather — which of these aligns with Acme’s procurement/finance approval process? (2) Stephanie — can CS confirm we can automate prefix caching updates during the Sept sale?

If helpful, we can do a quick 20-minute call to walk through the numbers and the contract redlines.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: commit_amendment_redline.pdf
message_4_subject: Re: Pricing options: 2.5x commit vs 12-month uplift — ACME
message_4_body:
Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple of notes from procurement:
- We prefer the 12-month committed uplift for budget predictability, but we need the effective per-token rate at $0.00026 to get sign-off from finance.
- The included quarterly 7-day burst window is a big value-add; can we limit the activation notice to 48 hours rather than a week? Our ops schedule changes rapidly during promotions.

If you can update the redline with the $0.00026 rate and the 48-hour activation notice for burst windows, I’ll fast-track with legal this week. Also, can you provide an estimate for monthly overage charges if we exceed the committed amount (thresholds at 10% steps)?

Heather
Director, Platform Ops, Acme Retail
message_5_subject: Re: Pricing options: 2.5x commit vs 12-month uplift — ACME
message_5_body:
Heather — appreciate the clarity. Short answers:
- We can accept $0.00026/token for a 12-month committed uplift, pending final legal language. I’ve updated the redline and attached it (commit_amendment_redline.pdf).
- Burst activation: we’ll change the activation notice to 48 hours and document allowable activation windows in the runbook.
- Overage model: 0–10% = no charge (grace buffer), 10–25% = charged at 1.25x committed rate, >25% = 1.6x committed rate. We can include an optional pre-pay top-up to avoid overage charges if you prefer predictable billing.

Next steps I propose: I’ll upload the revised amendment to DocuSign for signature once we confirm the legal phrasing. Sofia/Stephanie — can you confirm if we should route the DocuSign to Heather + Acme legal (heather@acme-retail.com, legal@acme-retail.com) and copy finance (finance@acme-retail.com)?

If yes, I’ll create the DocuSign this afternoon.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: commit_amendment_redline.pdf (updated)
message_6_subject: Re: Pricing options: 2.5x commit vs 12-month uplift — ACME (DocuSign ready)
message_6_body:
Heather — great, thanks for the go-ahead. We’ll route the DocuSign to the addresses you confirmed (Heather + legal + finance). Ben will enable the 48-hour burst activation language and the $0.00026/token rate in the amendment. Stephanie — CS will schedule a short ops runbook session the week of Aug 10 to implement prefix cache configuration and pre-warming steps for the Sept sale.

I’ll mark the HubSpot deal ACME-2026-Q3-EXP-42 as 'contract_pending_signature' and add the redline and forecast files to the record. Once the DocuSign is signed we’ll trigger the provisioning workflow to increase the committed quota and confirm scheduled burst windows.

Proposed timeline summary:
- 7/07: Final amendment uploaded to DocuSign (Ben)
- 7/09: Target signature by Acme legal/finance
- 7/15: Internal provisioning & ETA for commit start date (if signed)
- Aug 10 week: Ops runbook & pre-warm test
- Sept 01: Anticipated peak promotion window

Thanks — I’ll send the DocuSign link when it’s live.

—Sofia
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
